Project Overview • Motivation
Problem Statement & Project Objectives
  • Vulnerable IoT Deployments:
    Smart hostels use microcontrollers for door locks and power monitoring, but chips often lack memory for encryption.
  • Critical Threat Surface:
    Cleartext telemetry leaks tenant routines; unauthenticated channels let attackers forge door unlock commands.
  • Simulation Objective:
    Build a high-fidelity 8-device hostel testbed in Python without requiring physical hardware.
  • Dual-Mode Architecture:
    Directly evaluate an unmitigated baseline against an advanced, defense-in-depth hardened implementation.
  • Empirical Verification:
    Execute 6 realistic cyber attacks and quantitatively measure defense mitigation.
Baseline Insecure Execution: 6/6 Attacks Succeeded (100% Exploit Rate)

System Design • Fleet Topology
Decoupled 5-Stage System Architecture
  • 8 Simulated Nodes:
    2 RFID door locks (gate & warden), 2 temperature sensors, 2 energy meters, and 2 PIR motion sensors.
  • Virtual Wire & Attacker Tap:
    In-memory publish/subscribe transport layer with packet interception, injection, and tampering hooks.
  • Secure Gateway Broker:
    Validates client JWT tokens, checks HMAC integrity tags, and throttles floods via token buckets.
  • Hardened Cloud API:
    Flask backend with encrypted SQLite storage and tamper-evident forensic audit logging.
  • Deterministic Clock:
    Injected virtual clock allows sub-second, 100% deterministic testing with zero thread sleeps.
End-to-End Layered Architecture: Devices, Wire, Broker, Cloud, and Dashboard

Module 2 • Cryptographic Hardening
Authenticated Encryption & Key Management
  • AES-256-GCM Encryption:
    Symmetric authenticated encryption with fresh 12-byte initialization vectors (nonces) per message.
  • Associated Data (AD):
    Cryptographically binds device ID and MQTT topic directly to the ciphertext.
  • HMAC-SHA256 Integrity:
    Canonicalized length-prefixed tags guarantee messages cannot be altered in-flight.
  • ECDSA P-256 Signatures:
    Asymmetric secp256r1 curve digital signatures for non-repudiable physical door unlock commands.
  • Micro-Benchmark:
    AES-GCM latency is under 0.05 ms per packet, proving suitability for low-power IoT chips.
Empirical Latency Benchmark: AES-256-GCM vs. ChaCha20-Poly1305
HostelGuard • Module 2Slide 5 of 12
Module 3 • Access Control
Identity Registry, Bcrypt & Role-Based Access
  • Bcrypt Password Hashing:
    Adaptive cost factor 12 (~4096 rounds) makes offline dictionary cracking computationally infeasible.
  • Progressive Account Lockout:
    5 consecutive failed logins trigger an automated 60-second administrative freeze.
  • Role-Based Access (RBAC):
    Warden (Admin & Doors), Technician (Telemetry only), Student (Aggregated Temp only).
  • Broker Gateway Enforcement:
    Validates client JWT role claims before permitting topic subscriptions or publishes.
  • Zero Privilege Escalation:
    Technicians and students cannot issue door unlock commands under any condition.
Terminal Execution: Secure Mode Authentication & Role Enforcement
HostelGuard • Module 3Slide 6 of 12
Module 3 • Privacy Preservation
Data Privacy: Differential Privacy & K-Anonymity
  • Student Privacy Risk:
    Continuous telemetry reveals student occupancy, sleep schedules, and room presence.
  • Data Minimisation:
    Strips quasi-identifiers (room numbers, device serials) from student-facing feeds.
  • Laplace Differential Privacy:
    Injects calibrated mathematical noise (epsilon=1.0) into numeric temperature feeds.
  • K-Anonymity (k=3):
    Suppresses sensor groupings containing fewer than 3 readings to prevent re-identification.
  • Preserved Utility:
    Guarantees mathematical privacy while retaining building-wide thermal management utility.
Laplace Noise Distribution and K-Anonymity Cluster Preservation

Module 4 • Cloud Service & UI
Hardened Cloud Service & Live Operations Console
  • Stateless JWT Authentication:
    Cloud API verifies HS256-signed bearer tokens with strict 1-hour expiration.

Module 4 • Real-Time Case Study
Mirai Botnet (2016) vs HostelGuard Mitigations
  • Mirai Botnet Impact:
    Compromised 600,000+ IoT cameras/routers to launch historic 1.2 Tbps DDoS floods.
  • Root Cause: Default Passwords:
    Mirai scanned telnet ports using a dictionary of only 61 factory credentials.
  • HostelGuard Defense 1:
    Eliminates default passwords via mandatory Bcrypt salted hashing.
  • HostelGuard Defense 2:
    Progressive lockout terminates automated credential scans after 5 attempts.
  • HostelGuard Defense 3:
    Broker token-bucket rate limiter throttles traffic bursts and drops excess egress.
Safety Fault Tree: Mapping Systemic IoT Vulnerabilities Exploited by Mirai

Integration • Security Benchmark
Red Team vs Blue Team Hardening Results
  • Replay Attack:
    SUCCEEDED (3/3 Replayed) → BLOCKED by sequence counter & 30s window.
  • Spoofing Attack:
    SUCCEEDED (Command Delivered) → BLOCKED by HMAC tag & ECDSA signature.
  • Credential Brute-Force:
    SUCCEEDED (Cracked in 6 tries) → BLOCKED by Bcrypt & account lockout.
  • Flooding (DoS):
    SUCCEEDED (50/50 Processed) → BLOCKED by rate limiter (dropped 30/50).
  • Wire Sniffing & Tampering:
    SUCCEEDED (Plaintext read/altered) → BLOCKED by AES-GCM encryption.
  • Security Score:
    Insecure: 0/100 (Grade F) → Secure: 100/100 (Grade A+).
Hardening Benchmark: Attack Success Rate (1 = Breached, 0 = Blocked)
